comparison: Perfect agreement on Halo-TDP-43 knock-in line generation and validation (C3, C33, C47-C57). Both evaluations find the tool well-characterized and foundational. OpenEval notes lower expression of tagged vs untagged protein but considers it acceptable; peer reviewers raised no concerns about this limitation.

Strong agreement on CRISPRi screen design and execution (C4, C34, C58-C63). Both evaluations praise the methodology as rigorous and novel. OpenEval emphasizes BORC identification in neurons (C64, C70); peer reviewers focus on overall screen quality without specifically addressing C64 or C70.

Both address meta-analysis approach but with different emphases. OpenEval R3 focuses on analytical framework and pathway identification (C5, C35, C71-C82, C161-C163). Peer R4 emphasizes the meta-analysis context (C5, C35, C72, C75-C76, C79, C162-C166) and broader impact. Both support the approach but peer review highlights generalizability more.

Both address BORC validation but from different angles. OpenEval R4 emphasizes validation methods and 58% validation rate (C37, C64, C84-C87, C89-C90, C93-C95). Peer R3 focuses on BORC as a novel finding with cell-type specificity (C8, C37, C64, C80, C93, C95). Both strongly support BORC findings.

Complete agreement that BORC affects TDP-43 at protein but not mRNA level (C40-C41, C112-C113, C115-C117). Both evaluations accept the qPCR and RNA-seq data and the post-transcriptional mechanism inference. No concerns raised by either evaluation.

Agreement on paradoxical half-life findings from dSILAC (C10, C42, C138, C140, C173). Both evaluations acknowledge the counterintuitive result that decreased protein correlates with longer half-life. OpenEval notes mechanism remains unclear; peer reviewers explicitly note the paradox but accept the data quality.

Strong agreement on lysosomal drug experiments (C43-C44, C99-C102, C106-C107, C179-C180). Both evaluations support the conclusion that active, properly localized lysosomes are required for TDP-43 regulation. OpenEval emphasizes drug panel specificity; peer reviewers focus on mechanistic implications.

Agreement on TDP-43/lysosome co-trafficking observations (C110-C111). OpenEval explicitly evaluates the live imaging data; peer reviewers implicitly accept these findings as part of the mechanistic link between BORC, lysosomes, and TDP-43. Both support the conclusions.

Agreement on absence of cryptic exons despite TDP-43 reduction (C122-C123). OpenEval notes this negative result is important for interpretation and that remaining TDP-43 (~60%) is sufficient for splicing. Peer reviewers treat this as an interesting paradox requiring future work rather than a flaw.

Both address alternative polyadenylation analysis (C124-C128). OpenEval R10 emphasizes the negative result for TDP-43 polyA changes ruling out this mechanism. Peer R12 accepts RNA-seq findings broadly, supporting the post-transcriptional narrative without specific critique of polyadenylation analysis.

Agreement on SunTag translation assay results (C131-C133). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to acknowledged limitations of overexpression system and inability to definitively rule out translation hypothesis. Peer reviewers accept the negative result and shift to degradation focus without criticism of the approach.

Minimal overlap. OpenEval R12 addresses phosphoproteomics and pathway validation (C143-C152). Peer R14 only mentions cross-validation with published data (C143). Both support the proteomics findings but peer review provides less detailed evaluation of this aspect.

Both address discrepancies between Halo-tagged and endogenous TDP-43. OpenEval R13 rates as UNCERTAIN due to concerns about generalizability for specific pathways (C91-C92). Peer R10 accepts validation approach (C86-C87, C90-C91) without raising concerns, focusing on BORC consistency across both assays.

Partial overlap on validation results. OpenEval R4 emphasizes 58% validation rate and multiple validation methods (C86-C87, C90). Peer R10 accepts validation strategy (C86-C87, C90-C91) as part of overall convincing evidence. Both support the validation approach.

Partial overlap on RNA-seq analysis. OpenEval R9 addresses differential expression and GO enrichment (C119-C120) as part of cryptic exon analysis. Peer R12 accepts RNA-seq findings (C119-C120, C125-C128) as supporting post-transcriptional mechanism. Both evaluations support the RNA-seq data quality.

Minimal overlap on study implications. OpenEval R14 addresses major conclusions and therapeutic potential (C6, C12-C13, C45-C46, C165-C166, C180, C188-C189, C199-C201, C203, C205). Peer R4 mentions generalizability (C165-C166) as part of meta-analysis impact. Both support the broader significance.

OpenEval R15 evaluates background and literature context claims (C1-C2, C14-C32, C96, C187, C198) as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers did not separately evaluate background claims, focusing instead on novel findings and methodology.

Peer R13 accepts pathway-level findings from the screen (C66-C67) as part of broader results. OpenEval did not create a separate result for these specific pathway claims, though they may be implicitly covered in screen evaluation (R2).
